stories.summary: Global climate talks opening in Turkey on Monday are unlikely to produce new emissions targets, Singapore's environment minister Grace Fu said, urging negotiators to focus on implementing measures already agreed; nearly 200 countries are meeting in Antalya for the 12-day COP31 conference.
stories.title: Climate talks should focus on implementation, not new targets, Singapore says
stories.why: Singapore's position at COP31 — delivery over new pledges — as the first climate summit since the US left the Paris Agreement.

stories.summary: Singapore's 2026 haze episode has cost the economy an estimated S$2.32 billion as at 31 Oct, about 4% more than the inflation-adjusted 2015 bill, despite fewer hazy days and a lower average PSI, according to NTU's Euston Quah and SUSS's Eugene Or.
stories.title: Haze in 2026 estimated to cost Singapore S$2.32 billion, up 4% from 2015: experts
stories.why: The final bill for the worst haze in a decade — and a test of the tougher transboundary haze law passed last week.

stories.summary: SIA unveiled its next-generation long-haul cabins on 6 Nov, including First Class centre seats that combine into an 80-by-60-inch double bed, as part of a S$2 billion upgrade across all four classes; the new seats enter service from the second half of 2027 on Boeing 777-9s and retrofitted A350-900s.
stories.title: Singapore Airlines unveils new First Class suite with the 'largest double bed in commercial aviation'
stories.why: The national carrier's biggest cabin overhaul — though the rollout has already slipped twice.

stories.summary: The Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group pulled into Singapore on Friday for a port visit — carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt, cruiser USS Chosin and destroyers USS Paul Hamilton and USS Decatur — before transiting the Malacca Strait toward the Middle East, where it will become the third US carrier group in the region.
stories.title: USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group pulls into Singapore
stories.why: A US supercarrier in Singapore's waters, en route to the Iran standoff — and a visible sign of the South China Sea-to-Gulf shift.

stories.summary: Nvidia's board said on Sunday it has launched an independent investigation into reports CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, after US intelligence concluded Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security; Huang told staff he had an affair with her. The board said it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised.
stories.title: Nvidia opens probe into CEO's affair with suspected Chinese spy
stories.why: The Megaspeed affair now reaches Nvidia's boardroom — and puts Singapore's role in the chip-smuggling scrutiny back in the spotlight.

stories.summary: Apple CEO John Ternus is pressing software chief Craig Federighi to speed up Siri's roadmap, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported on 8 Nov, with a more agentic Siri — one that pursues goals rather than answering one-off requests — possible as early as 2027; first-party app control arrives in iOS 27.3 in December, third-party support in spring 2027.
stories.title: Apple wants Siri to act more like an AI agent as early as next year, Gurman reports
stories.why: Apple is racing to catch OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse in always-on agents — the class of assistant Singapore just warned consumers about.

stories.summary: Nvidia now requires Southeast Asian cloud providers seeking its Cloud Partner status to enrol in its Fleet Intelligence system, which can track the location of AI accelerators, Bloomberg reported on 6 Nov, as Washington presses on chips reaching China through regional routes; Nvidia has also cut about half its pre-approved Asian buyers.
stories.title: Nvidia ties Southeast Asia Cloud Partner status to chip-location tracking
stories.why: Export controls are now enforced through partner perks — and Singapore sits at the centre of the transshipment scrutiny.

stories.summary: From 7 Nov, text from seven Grok models via xAI's API carries an invisible statistical watermark by default, under the EU AI Act's transparency rules; team admins can opt out per model only by confirming a legal exception applies. The change covers the developer API only, not the Grok app or X.
stories.title: xAI switches on invisible watermarking for Grok API text by default
stories.why: The first default-on watermarking at a frontier lab — a template for the EU's 2 December AI-transparency deadline.

stories.summary: Taiwan's regulator will cap intraday short-sale orders at 3% of average daily volume, down from 30%, and raise minimum short-sale margin to 130% from 90% from today, after the Taiex fell 12.2% last week, its worst since 2001; the NT$500 billion National Financial Stabilization Fund has been authorised to intervene, its tenth deployment since 2000.
stories.title: Taiwan curbs short selling and readies US$15b fund as AI rout triggers worst week since 2001
stories.why: Asia's emergency brake on the AI sell-off — and the test case for whether state backstops can steady chip markets.

stories.summary: South Korea's financial authorities will waive the rule requiring brokerages to hold collateral worth 140% of margin loans from today until 31 Jan, after the Kospi plunged 6% on Friday and briefly fell below 5,000, triggering a circuit breaker; the move aims to stop forced sales amplifying the sell-off.
stories.title: South Korea waives margin-loan collateral rule for three months to curb forced selling
stories.why: Seoul joins Taipei in emergency market support as the AI rout hits Asia's chip-heavy exchanges.

stories.summary: South Korea's Kospi is expected to open higher on Monday after Friday's 6.02% plunge to 5,059.69, its lowest close in about seven months, with US chip stocks rebounding — Nvidia up 2.78%, AMD 11.04% — and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 4.2%.
stories.title: Kospi eyes rebound after Friday's 6% plunge as US chip stocks recover
stories.why: Monday's open is the first test of whether the rout has bottomed — or just paused before Tuesday's US CPI.

stories.summary: Bitcoin traded near $75,100–76,000 on Monday morning, down from $81,000 midweek, after US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost a net $1.28 billion in the week to 6 Nov — the heaviest weekly outflow in four months, led by BlackRock's IBIT — with traders eyeing Tuesday's US CPI print.
stories.title: Bitcoin slips toward $75,000 as ETFs lose $1.28 billion in a week
stories.why: Crypto's institutional exit is accelerating alongside the AI-stock rout, with $80,000 now the recovery marker to watch.

stories.summary: Standard Chartered reported a 46% rise in third-quarter net profit to US$1.5 billion and raised its full-year guidance, with CEO Bill Winters saying at a Hong Kong media round table on Friday that geopolitical fragmentation is 'an advantage' because it drives demand from multinationals for cross-border services.
stories.title: Standard Chartered profits from geopolitical fragmentation as earnings soar: CEO
stories.why: A bank profiting from the very fragmentation rattling markets — and a sign of where Asia's wealth flows are heading.

stories.summary: President Trump told CNN a fresh US military campaign against Iran is 'highly unlikely' but warned forces are ready, saying three aircraft carriers are 'fully locked and loaded' and that the US has identified targets including power plants and 38 bridges; he claimed Iran retains only 10% of its missile capacity after earlier strikes.
stories.title: Trump says fresh Iran strikes 'highly unlikely' — but keeps military option on the table
stories.why: The clearest signal yet on whether the Iran war restarts or winds down — as a third carrier group sails for the Gulf.

stories.summary: Exercise Koalicja begins today in Nowa Dęba, Poland, running to 22 Nov, with about 2,800 troops from 11 nations rehearsing how a European-led Multinational Force Ukraine would deploy once fighting ends — testing movement, command and counter-drone work, without US troops or heavy armour.
stories.title: Coalition of the Willing begins first large-scale exercise in Poland
stories.why: Europe's Ukraine force moves from paper to the training ground — the first credibility test of a post-war security guarantee without Washington.

stories.summary: Defence AI firm Shield AI agreed on 5 Nov to acquire radar maker Echodyne in a deal worth up to $5.3 billion, moving into counter-drone systems, and is raising $2.5 billion including a Series H at a $28.8 billion valuation; the deal is expected to close in early 2027.
stories.title: Shield AI to buy radar maker Echodyne in $5.3 billion deal
stories.why: The biggest defence-tech consolidation of the year — autonomy software buying the sensors that spot drones.

stories.summary: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Sunday he is 'a hard yes' on impeaching Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of abusing power and engineering the 'reckless and costly war of choice in Iran'; Republican Rep. Thomas Massie plans to reintroduce an eight-article privileged resolution as early as Monday, which would force a House vote within two legislative days.
stories.title: Top House Democrat 'a hard yes' on impeaching Hegseth
stories.why: The Iran war's political fallout reaches the Pentagon's top job — with a floor vote possible this week.

stories.summary: A wave of false claims followed the 7 Nov shooting in Kraków that killed six, with Poland's NASK Disinformation Analysis Centre flagging more than 2,000 accounts spreading narratives that the gunman was Ukrainian or that the government staged the attack; posts peaked at over 200 million views on Saturday evening. The attacker was in fact a 24-year-old Polish national with far-right ties, police said.
stories.title: Poland hit by disinformation wave after Kraków shooting
stories.why: A textbook case of a tragedy being weaponised within minutes — and of a state counter-disinformation unit working in real time.

stories.summary: A Russian influence operation identified by OpenAI as 'Dark Clark' used AI to impersonate education authorities in Peru and Ecuador, tricking schools into hosting events designed to sow political discord, including a fake National Day of Cultural and Linguistic Diversity; the campaign is linked to entities associated with the late Yevgeniy Prigozhin.
stories.title: Russian influence operation targets Latin American schools with AI-generated disinformation
stories.why: AI-generated disinformation aimed at schoolchildren — the influence playbook reaching a new low, and a new audience.

stories.summary: Taiwan President William Lai warned that disinformation, smear campaigns and cyberattacks on candidates' websites will increase ahead of the 28 Nov local elections, saying large numbers of suspicious social media accounts — registered with overseas phone numbers but listing Taiwan as their location — have recently appeared.
stories.title: Lai details online disinformation tactics ahead of election
stories.why: A head of state naming the disinformation playbook in advance — the same tactics seen in this cycle's US midterms and the Kraków aftermath.

tldr: Singapore: COP31 opens with Grace Fu urging implementation over new targets, the 2026 haze is costed at S$2.32b, and a US carrier strike group is in port ahead of its Gulf deployment.
Technology: Nvidia's board opened a probe into CEO Jensen Huang over the alleged Chinese spy affair, Apple is pushing Siri toward agentic AI, and Nvidia tightened chip tracking across Southeast Asia.

Finance: Taiwan and South Korea both pulled emergency market levers today after last week's AI rout, the Kospi eyes a rebound, Bitcoin ETFs bled $1.28b — and StanChart said geopolitical fragmentation is boosting its profits.

Defence: Trump says fresh Iran strikes are 'highly unlikely' with three carriers ready, Europe's Ukraine force starts its first exercise in Poland, Shield AI bought Echodyne for $5.3b, and the top House Democrat backed impeaching Pentagon chief Hegseth.

Information warfare: A disinformation wave followed the Kraków shooting, a Russian AI-generated influence operation targeted schools in Latin America, and Taiwan's president warned of rising disinformation ahead of local elections.
